analysis: Examined four changed files. (1) ClusterRuntimeFactsCommand.swift (hidden dev/release CLI): adds --release-candidates and --list-release-models and makes --app optional. validate() enforces that --app is given with exactly one of --model or --release-candidates, and that --list-release-models takes no other option. The release path round-trips the canonical bytes through the strict decoder (line 57) before writing. Notes go to stderr. The command is metadata-only (no network, secrets or GPU), so no new trust boundary is crossed. The supplied evidence does not show how ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts.release, candidates(in:) or the public-model declaration are implemented. Whether the facts give the coordinator adequate qualification evidence (T-054/A-017) is therefore unverified and belongs to the platform. (2) ClusterSetupWizardCommand.swift line 106: passes request.scope into service.wizard.servingScope. This is a settings plumbing change. The definition of the scope and how it is enforced downstream are not visible. The question for the next pass is whether the default and a missing scope fail closed, and whether scope can widen what is served beyond the prior behavior. (3) MemberFixtureServicePart.swift: test-only fixture writing a health file when an environment variable is set, using .withoutOverwriting in a test-controlled directory. No production impact. (4) PlacementSetupCheck.swift: test adjusted to a new publicModels parameter on publicTrafficLine. The test asserts that an empty public declaration plus no record yields notYetQualified, which is consistent with fail-closed behavior. The production signature change is not shown. No concrete security regression is identified; the residual uncertainty is about the unseen ClusterPairServingGrants/ClusterPublicModels/servingScope implementations.
